body: The Russian invasion to Ukraine raised, perhaps more than any other time, the question as to whether Japan should or should not go nuclear. On March 25, former prime minster Shinzo Abe shocked Japan, and the surrounding region, when he said in an interview with Sankei Shimbun that Japan should consider nuclear weapons and “start discussing whether to seek a nuclear sharing arrangement similar to the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation’s nuclear deterrence policy”.

After the war, Japan adopted the Three Non-Nuclear Principles, which stipulate non-possession, non-production, and non-introduction of nuclear weapons in its territories. Japan is still politically firmly stuck to these principles in accordance with its Peace Constitution. Former prime minister, Yoshihide Suga, vowed not only to prevent the proliferation of nuclear weapons, but also to free the world of all nuclear arms. This Japanese sensitivity to nuclear technology was further reinforced after the Fukushima disaster in 2011.
